title: Lachman v. Philadelphia Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied Lachman's appeal and upheld Philadelphia Presbytery's affirmance of Calvary Session's judgment finding him guilty on all fifth-, sixth-, and ninth-commandment charges and suspending him from the ruling eldership. No other relief was granted; the concurrence only suggested future change-of-venue practice.
first_summary: A ruling elder appealed his Session conviction for fifth-, sixth-, and ninth-commandment violations, arguing the prosecution used only documentary evidence without witnesses. The SJC denied the appeal, finding sufficient evidence in his letters and admissions and that the Session followed Matthew 18.
summary: A ruling elder convicted by his Session of fifth-, sixth-, and ninth-commandment violations challenged the conviction because the prosecution presented no live witness and relied on his own letters. The SJC denied the appeal and upheld Presbytery's affirmance, holding that the documents, Lachman's acknowledgments of writing them, and defense witnesses supplied sufficient proof; the Session also followed Matthew 18 with patience. A concurrence urged change-of-venue procedures for small-Session bias cases, but noted Lachman never requested a reference or challenged the court before trial.
